content:
Ben Carlson: hey all, day 1 hiccup. following the k8s quickstart but `kubectl get ns demo-space` returns namespaces "demo-space" not found. i'm on windows (powershell) and used the Okta SSO; anything obvious i'm missing?

Rani Sethi: welcome Ben! :wave: on Windows KUBECONFIG handling can be weird. run `echo $env:KUBECONFIG` in pwsh and `kubectl config get-contexts`. also verify `kubelogin` didn't replace your user entry.

Ben Carlson: `echo $env:KUBECONFIG` -> `C:\Users\ben\.kube\config;C:\Users\ben\.kube\okta-config` (semicolon). `kubectl config get-contexts` shows `redwood-dev` current, user looks like `ben@okta`.

Rani Sethi: semicolon is normal on Windows. Two likely issues: 1) namespace exists but your RBAC prevents listing it, or 2) your merged kubeconfig picked up an `admin@work` authinfo from another file. Try `kubectl config view --minify --flatten` and `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n demo-space`.

Ben Carlson: `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n demo-space` -> no. `kubectl --as=system:serviceaccount:demo-space:ci-sa get pods -n demo-space` -> forbidden: cannot impersonate.

Rani Sethi: yep RBAC. For new hires we usually either add a namespaced RoleBinding for your Okta user or give a short-lived SA token. Which works for you now?

Ben Carlson: RoleBinding is fine for now, want to finish the tutorial. I'll switch to SA token later for automation.

Rani Sethi: cool. @eng-infra-bot can you open an infra request to bind `ben@okta` to `edit` in `demo-space`? Note: windows user, quick grant, TTL 24h.

eng-infra-bot: Created INFRA-4699: "new-hire Ben Carlson - demo-space access". Assignee: @platform-oncall. ETA 45m.

platform-oncall: Hi Ben 44b applied a namespaced RoleBinding (edit) in `demo-space` for `ben@okta` with TTL 24h. Try `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n demo-space` and `kubectl get pods -n demo-space` now.

Ben Carlson: running checks... `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n demo-space` -> yes. `kubectl get pods -n demo-space` -> lists 9 pods. woo! thanks so much :tada:

Rani Sethi: great. follow-up tips: 1) if your KUBECONFIG merge is picking wrong authinfo, you can create a dedicated context for okta with `kubectl config set-credentials ben-okta --exec-command=kubelogin --exec-arg=get-token` etc, or just set `KUBECONFIG` to the okta file for interactive sessions. 2) for CI use SA token: `kubectl create token ci-sa -n demo-space` and set a local kubeconfig user.

Ben Carlson: saved both snippets. quick question: where do i mark this step done in the checklist?

platform-oncall: I've linked INFRA-4699 to ONBOARD-236 and updated the checklist. You can mark the K8s access step complete.

onboarding-bot: \u2705 K8s access granted and linked INFRA-4699 to ONBOARD-236. Checklist updated.

Ben Carlson: marked it. thanks everyone for the fast help!
